Key Research Thinking Patterns: Systems Integration and Prototyping: Building functional, real-world testbeds by combining disparate hardware and software components. (e.g. Integrating DSRC (OBU/RSU) hardware, an OBD-II (Crosschasm) reader, a laptop server, and a Dynamic Message Sign to create a working connected vehicle alert system).

Pragmatic, Constraint-Base Optimization: Designing solutions tailored to real-world limitations (like low bandwidth or existing hardware) rather than for purely theoretical performance. (e.g. Using an adaptive frame-dropping strategy for video surveillance that maintains high spatial quality (needed for monitoring) at the expense of temporal resolution, which is less critical and solves low-bandwidth network issues).

Data Fusion for Correlative Analysis: Combining multiple, distinct datasets to uncover new relationships and support data-driven decisions. (e.g. Merging the national FARS database with Oklahoma's roadway inventory and collision databases (SAFE-T) to analyze how specific road characteristics correlate with fatal crashes).

Hardware-Software Co-Design: Identifying software bottlenecks and designing specialized hardware to accelerate or bypass them. (e.g. Proposing a novel hardware circuit (Shared Context Unit) to manage thread context switching, aiming to drastically reduce the high latency and overhead associated with traditional OS-based context switching).
Summary Description: Dr. Ronald Barnes's research integrates computer architecture with Intelligent Transportation Systems (ITS) and traffic safety data analysis. In architecture, he designs novel hardware for low-overhead thread-context switching and investigates performance gains from runahead pre-execution in in-order processors. His ITS work focuses on practical, constraint-based solutions, including adaptive video rate control for surveillance over low-bandwidth networks and prototyping DSRC-based connected vehicle systems for real-time driver safety alerts. He also specializes in data fusion, developing integrated databases from FARS and roadway inventories to enable Blackspot and Systemic Analysis for improved highway safety planning.
